Bill number: HB0522
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 386
 By Taylor

 HOUSE BILL 522

 By Reedy

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 16;
 Title 37 and Title 49, relative to student behavior.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Early Behavioral Intervention

 and Reporting Act."

 (b) As used in this section, "early warning signs" means evidence of a student's

 safety, health, or behavioral issues and includes, but is not limited to, indicators of a

 student engaging in or being the victim of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyber-

 bullying; making or receiving threats of violence; and exhibiting signs of substance

 abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system that teachers and school staff must use to input data of early warning signs

 demonstrated by students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school. Each LEA and

 public charter school shall ensure that each teacher and school staff member is trained

 to identify early warning signs and on how to input data into the computer-based system.

 (d) The computer-based system implemented pursuant to subsection (c) must:

 (1) Align with the requirements in § 49-6-4503; the School Discipline Act,

 compiled in part 41 of this chapter; and the school safety plans adopted by the

 LEA or public charter school pursuant to the Schools Against Violence in

 Education (SAVE) Act, compiled in part 8 of this chapter;

 (2) Include a database that is capable of receiving and maintaining

 student data entered by teachers and school staff on the early warning signs

 demonstrated by its students; and

 (3) Immediately notify the LEA's or public charter school's personnel

 serving on the LEA's or public charter school's threat assessment team created

 pursuant to § 49-6-2701 when an early warning sign is entered into the system

 for a student.

 (e) The LEA or public charter school personnel receiving a notification of an

 early warning sign of a student pursuant to subdivision (d)(3) shall review the

 notification, and any notifications of the student previously received, and determine

 whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior of an early warning

 sign.

 (f) Each LEA and public charter school shall annually submit a report to the

 department of education summarizing the data collected in the immediately preceding

 school year and the interventions provided, if any.

 (g) Reports made pursuant to this section must comply with the Family

 Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (20 U.S.C. § 1232g); § 10-7-504; the Data

 Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, compiled in chapter 1, part 7 of this

 title; and all other relevant privacy laws.

 (h) If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or public charter school is

 not complying with this section, then the commissioner may withhold state funds, in an

 amount determined by the commissioner, from the LEA or public charter school until the

 LEA or public charter school is in compliance with this section.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2701, is amended by adding

"and public charter school" after "Each LEA", adding "or public charter school" after "LEA"

wherever it appears in the section, adding "or public charter school's" after "LEA's" in subsection

(b), adding "or public charter school governing body" after "local board of education" in

subsection (e), and adding "or the director of the public charter school" after "the director of

schools" in subsection (e).

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2702(b), is amended by adding

"or public charter school" after "LEA" and adding "or public charter school's" after "LEA's".

 SECTION 4. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to use a computer-based system for reporting students’ early warning signs, such as bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health concerns, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts. Teachers and school staff would have to enter observed signs and receive training to identify them and use the system. The system would have to align with specified school discipline and safety requirements, keep the entered data, and immediately alert the LEA’s or school’s threat assessment team when a sign is entered. Team personnel would review the alert and any earlier alerts for that student and decide whether further action is needed.

Each LEA and public charter school would also have to report annually to the Department of Education on data collected during the prior school year and any interventions provided. Reports would have to comply with specified student privacy and other laws. If the education commissioner found an LEA or public charter school out of compliance, the commissioner could withhold a determined amount of state funds until compliance. The bill would also amend existing provisions on threat assessment teams by adding public charter schools and their governing bodies and directors to the text; it does not state the other requirements of those provisions. The bill would take effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: students’ early warning signs, such as bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health concerns, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts
assessments.rationale: Conveys several nonexclusive examples, but omits the broader safety, health, or behavioral definition and the express coverage of victims, recipients of threats, harassment, intimidation, and cyber-bullying.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to use a computer-based system for reporting students’ early warning signs, such as bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health concerns, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts. Teachers and school staff would have to enter observed signs and receive training to identify them and use the system.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the system requirement for each LEA and public charter school and mandatory data entry by teachers and school staff.

assessments.summary_quote: Teachers and school staff would have to enter observed signs and receive training to identify them and use the system.
assessments.rationale: Conveys required training for teachers and school staff in both identifying signs and using the reporting system.

assessments.summary_quote: The system would have to align with specified school discipline and safety requirements
assessments.rationale: Conveys mandatory alignment generally, but does not identify § 49-6-4503, the School Discipline Act, or the schools’ safety plans adopted under SAVE.

assessments.summary_quote: The system would have to align with specified school discipline and safety requirements, keep the entered data
assessments.rationale: In the context of the preceding staff data-entry requirement, keeping the entered data conveys the required receiving and maintaining database function.

assessments.summary_quote: immediately alert the LEA’s or school’s threat assessment team when a sign is entered
assessments.rationale: Conveys the immediate notification trigger and the responsible threat assessment team recipients.

assessments.summary_quote: Team personnel would review the alert and any earlier alerts for that student and decide whether further action is needed.
assessments.rationale: Conveys review of both current and prior notifications and the determination whether further action is necessary.

assessments.rationale: Includes the reporting actors, recipient, annual frequency, reporting period, and interventions.

assessments.rationale: Conveys the commissioner's discretionary withholding authority, noncompliance condition, affected entities, and duration; the amount determination is conveyed in context.
